submissions.title: Manatee County issues one-year ban on data centers
submissions.excerpt: Commissioners voted unanimously to impose a 12-month moratorium on data centers
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Manatee County, FL adopted Ordinance 26-42, a 12-month moratorium on data center/large-load-customer permit applications (building permits, site plans, rezones, comprehensive plan amendments) in unincorporated county land, effective Sept 22, 2026. No tracked project is currently sited in Manatee County; flagging as a jurisdiction-level restriction relevant to future siting risk in the region. submissions.title: House passes ratepayer protection bill to limit data center cost shifts
submissions.excerpt: The House passed the Ratepayer Protection Act, 417-3, on Sept. 16
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: The U.S. House passed the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act 417-3 on Sept 16, 2026, which would require large energy loads (data centers >100 MW) to bear the cost of new grid/generation infrastructure needed to serve them rather than shifting it to existing ratepayers, and directs states to 'consider' adopting related cost-allocation standards. Now before the Senate — not yet law. National in scope, not tied to one tracked project; relevant context for every US project's interconnection economics. Caveat: WebFetch was blocked this run; excerpt drawn from search summary of multiple outlets (Utility Dive, NBC News, Energy & Commerce Committee) reporting the same 417-3 figure, not a page fetch I performed — verify before citing.

submissions.title: Imperial Valley utility adopts new pricing rules, putting data centers first for power cuts
submissions.excerpt: Our water was never meant for special interests or unchecked development
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Imperial Irrigation District (CA) adopted new large-load pricing rules requiring major energy users, including data centers, to fund their own infrastructure upgrades, pay a minimum monthly charge, and accept first-priority curtailment during power shortages. Attributed by IID as partly a response to data centers destabilizing Virginia's grid in 2024. Not tied to a specific tracked project (no tracked project currently sited in Imperial County, CA per the snapshot I could check), but material for any future Imperial Valley siting. Caveat: WebFetch was blocked this run; excerpt (the Board Chair quote) comes from a search summary, not a page fetch I performed — verify against source before citing.
